reviews.comment: Deceptive testing practices.  Told we would be given outputs to statistical software and asked to answer questions about output only.  Instead you have to frantically program for an hour and give up because there is no way to complete her exams in an hour.  Condescending when the class does poorly, but apparently she does this every year!

This is a very difficult professor. If you can avoid taking her, I would recommend it. This class was the most difficult stats class I have ever taken. I  only took this class to brush up on my stats (already took 2 at the Ph.D level) and regretted my decision. Practice test are not like the actual test although there are some similarities.

1. Cannot understand a word she says on her lectures
2. I have sent 6 emails - she has not responded to a single one 
3. Exams are not hard but are not straight forward this means that you truly gotta know your stuff if you wanna do good.
4. RESPOND TO MY EMAILS 24!%!$#!#!@%
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Does not care about students

1) Cant understand a word she says. (Language barriers)
2) Classic professor that will teach you and give hw on certain topics and add 2 or 3 knots to the exams making them hard as hell. So shes not evaluating her stuff shes evaluating your analytical capability of being smart and solving through her knots rather than the real class content.

Dr. Chen makes the midterm exam impossible to the extent that she had to curve it 50 points to avoid failing her class. Her notes are pretty useful, but her lectures are not good. She gives a very brief and vague overview but does not explain things well. She is very rude when students attend her office hours. I do not recommend taking this class.
An absolute horrible teacher.  I will avoid her class in the future. Very poor teaching methods.

I noticed Professor Chen was incorrect about a few things throughout the semester on their solutions to the exams and homework. Often answers would contradict what was taught in the class or is established in statistics. Class is also structured like an undergrad class and not a graduate one, thus making it hard to balance with weird policies.

This is my fourth degree and I've probably taken 30 or 40 college-level courses. This course was the worst anything i have ever seen. Dr. Chen was dismissive, disorganized, and hard to understand. We all began to just laugh as she would tell us how easy it all was and that she'd already explained everything. Our midterm was curved fifty points.

Dr. Chen is a good one. She explains concepts clearly. Her note is very good and sufficient. Know your homework and class examples very well and you get an A. Her exams are reasonable and based on class materials. Expect weekly homework that takes 2-3 hours to go through with a good understanding.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Rushes through lectures, obsessed with giving homework, provides a surplus of dots but does not connect them. This was a low point on the professor scale during my time at TAMU. She appears to take questions/comments personally and isnt receptive to our end of the learning experience. Not a bad person, but I would avoid her classes if I were you.

One time, I went to her office hours to ask her for help on a test review. I had completed 29 out of 30 questions on it and I just needed help on that one missing question. She immediately began to lecture me and said that I do not pay attention in class. Like what? Funny thing is, when other people asked her help after class, she helped them ASAP.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class is tough but doable. She does not try to trick you and everything you need to know is from the power points. Tutor John is helpful but I recommend only the test sessions. She gives out test reviews that are very helpful! There is some homeworks and occasional extra credit quizzes, they were never too difficult or long.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: If you're good at math, you'll do well. She has a mild accent. She is really funny. Her lectures are really clear, and if you don't want to go to class the power points will tell you everything you need to know. She posts practice tests, which help prepare you for the test. I highly taking stat 303 with her.

Hard class. The concepts were hard to understand, and Professor Chen didn't help. It was hard to understand her at times, and she always makes comments about how easy the class is when it's not. The tests are weighted weirdly/poorly so study hard! You get cheat sheets for the tests so that helps. She curves ALOT at the end so that may save you.
reviews.ratingTags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The class itelf is tough but she makes it as easy as possible. Tests only have around 16 questions which makes it difficult but her lectures and reviews help A LOT. Attendance isn't mandatory but she gives pop quizes that are due the same night and if you aren't in class that day they are tough. Tests have somewhat of a curve usually as well!
reviews.ratingTags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Although she has a very think accent, she is easy to understand and her lectures make sense. Homework and quizzes can occasionally be a bit much but they're not too bad. Tests have 14-16 questions so they can be a little difficult to do well on. She is very caring and helpful though.

I struggle with math, but was able to get an A in the class. Gives practice exams before the exam and they are usually structured very similar. I stopped going to class and would go to tutoring off campus (which helped me more than listening to Chen read off slides she posts online with a very thick accent). Still the best STATS prof for sure.
reviews.ratingTags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: She has an accent but it is easy to get used to. Weekly online homework and surprise quizzes assigned on Fridays. Allows cheat sheets for exams which definitely makes the class easier. Kinda tough for people who struggle with math but is easily doable.

Allows cheatsheets on all tests&final. HW isn't bad. 7 attempts do get right answer. Can skip class. If you skip, be sure to check to see if she post a quiz for that day. She'll open a quiz after class and close it at midnight. One of the easier profs. Accent isn't too bad. I recommend making a groupme for the class for homework help and questions.
